html:
Michael Psellos was a Byzantine courtier, philosopher and historian, born in Constantinople in 1017 or 1018. He served and advised a run of emperors, and his history, the Chronographia, is the main inside account of the 11th-century court.

He rose as a secretary and became a leading figure under Constantine IX Monomachos, who made him "consul of the philosophers", head of philosophy teaching in the capital. He revived the study of Plato and the Neoplatonists alongside Aristotle, and his love of pagan thought sometimes brought him under suspicion. He became a monk for a while when his place at court was unsafe, then came back.

The Chronographia runs from Basil II to Michael VII Doukas, his own pupil, with sharp personal portraits of emperors and empresses, among them Zoe. Psellos was close to power under Michael VII in the years after the defeat at Manzikert in 1071, and his name suffered for it. He is thought to have died in 1078, though some say later.
